title: anthill-claude: in-session 'Now' pane showing active backlog items and their sessions
summary: anthill-claude mod: docked Now pane (active + validation rows from the CLI's --json), key chips under transcript rows, detail view on press, hover card, status line, /ant command.
value: Phase 4b of Backlog v2: a mod Pane beside the chat rendering 'anthill backlog list --active --json' + 'anthill session list --json', refreshed on turn.complete, so a supervisor session sees what its workers hold without leaving Claude Code (the TUI Now mode covers the terminal case; this covers the in-session case)
verify: claude plugin validate and claude plugin test green in anthill-claude; pane renders list and detail from fixture JSON; chips drawn for ANT-N mentions in user and assistant rows

title: doctor: don't warn on pristine runtime-seed files (dispatch control/ledger)
value: Fresh scaffolds permanently show a derivation-status warning for .anthill/dispatch/control.md and ledger.md, which are runtime artifacts meant to hold placeholders until first use — the noise trains users to ignore doctor warnings

title: doctor backlog-valid reports violations without listing them, and disagrees with backlog validate
value: In battlehounds (CLI 0.0.8) 'anthill doctor' fails backlog-valid with '26 violations' while 'anthill backlog validate' prints 'ok: 76 items'; neither text nor --json output names the items or rules, so the failure cannot be acted on.

title: release.ps1 aborts after 'git push' under PowerShell 5.1 (git stderr treated as a terminating error)
value: The 0.1.0 release stopped right after pushing: with $ErrorActionPreference=Stop, git's normal stderr progress ('To github.com:…') became a NativeCommandError and the script never ran go install or the version check, leaving the release half-done until finished by hand. Capture git output (e.g. 2>&1 | Out-String or --quiet, or check $LASTEXITCODE only) so the push step cannot false-fail.

title: Validation instructions when submitting to validate state
value: A lot of tasks get completed but their acceptance critera depend on the user testing something, for matters of taste that cant be verified subjectively. Our model should work with this fact and make it easy for the user to confirm they were completed as intended, so we should have a way to leave some testing/verification instructions on the task itself so that it's self contained and can be picked up easily by the user later. Can build this into the cli verb for delivering it. Not all tasks should require this step, and if they do it should be noted at least by the time they are sent to implementation. Trying to deliver such a task should ask for the verification instructions so it cant be bypassed
